facts.title: energy isolation failure on P-7113

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was first aid or minor property damage.

defences.finding: Control ENERGY_SOURCE_IDENTIFICATION: the identification of every energy source for the task was never verified as effective, and the ICAM investigation classified this as an organisational factor.

Control LOAD_SUPPORT_FOR_MAINTENANCE: the mechanical support of a load during maintenance access was in place but did not perform, and the ICAM investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.

Control STORED_ENERGY_DISSIPATION: the dissipation or restraint of trapped and residual energy was in place but did not perform, and the ICAM investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.
Control ZERO_ENERGY_VERIFICATION: the proving zero energy before intrusive work had been bypassed, and the ICAM investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the mechanical support of a load during maintenance access on P-7113, M-7113 and TK-7104 and record the critical control verification before this task is next authorised.
Restore the proving zero energy before intrusive work on P-7113, M-7113 and TK-7104 and record the critical control verification before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in restoring plant to service, specifically handing back a partially completed isolation. P-7113 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during a statutory inspection while the identification of every energy source for the task was never verified as effective. The thermal energy involved is held as hot surface, and the recorded presentation was burn, ignition, scald.
response.summary: On 18 January 2018 an incident occurred on P-7113, M-7113 and TK-7104 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during a statutory inspection, releasing thermal energy held as hot surface.
